description: PROCESS-ENTER-KEY's ordered EVALUATE TRUE at app/cbl/COUSR01C.cbl:117-151, arm five of five, reached through the LOW-VALUES limb of the test: USRTYPEI is omitted from the payload entirely, which is a field never typed, so it arrives as LOW-VALUES in map storage rather than as spaces. The condition at :142 is = SPACES OR LOW-VALUES - two comparisons against figurative constants, not one emptiness test - so this case exercises the limb the twenty-spaces route does not, and app/cbl/COUSR01C.cbl:142-147 wins. An EVALUATE is ordered and the first matching WHEN wins, so the four earlier arms must stay silent, and they provably do: FNAMEI, LNAMEI, USERIDI and PASSWDI all arrive non-blank and valid, so :118, :124, :130 and :136 are each evaluated and each fails to match before :142 is reached. Message derivation, summed mechanically rather than eyeballed: the literal at :144-145 is 'User Type can NOT be empty...', which is 29 characters; the receiver WS-MESSAGE is PIC X(80), so a shorter literal is left-justified and right-padded, giving 29 + 51 spaces; then MOVE WS-MESSAGE TO ERRMSGO at :188 narrows into PIC X(78) at app/cpy-bms/COUSR01.CPY:164, and a COBOL alphanumeric MOVE truncates on the RIGHT, giving 29 + 49 spaces. Both widths are declared because the two-byte narrowing is observable only when both are compared; a translation that truncated on the left, or padded instead, would still satisfy one of them. MOVE -1 TO USRTYPEL at :146 places the cursor on User Type; USRTYPEL is a length item and therefore cursor metadata, which is why it is stated as cursorField and never as a payload member - the payload is the twelve xxxO items and nothing else. The arm raises WS-ERR-FLG at :143, so the guard IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON at :153 is false and the five MOVEs to SEC-USR-* at :154-158 and PERFORM WRITE-USER-SEC-FILE at :159 are all skipped. Hence expectedWrites is empty and USERIDI 'NEWUSR01' - deliberately none of the ten keys app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:L35-L44 seeds - must NOT appear in USRSEC. That absence is the substance of the case, and it is asserted positively rather than by omission: expectedFinalState pins all ten seeded rows byte-for-byte at CSUSR01Y's full 80-byte width, and expectedDatasets pins the FINAL_STATE row count at exactly ten, so a spurious eleventh row is a diff even though no row expectation addresses index 10. Exactly one SEND occurs, at :147, so there is exactly one screen and one message pair; the post-EVALUATE guard fails and there is no second send. The five screen fields keep what was received, which the copybook proves rather than assumes: COUSR1AO REDEFINES COUSR1AI at app/cpy-bms/COUSR01.CPY:91 overlays every xxxO item on its xxxI item byte-for-byte, and this arm performs neither INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS nor MOVE LOW-VALUES TO COUSR1AO, so USRTYPEO echoes back the very LOW-VALUES byte x'00' that was never typed. The six header fields are repainted by POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :214-233 on every SEND and never echoed: CCDA-TITLE01 and CCDA-TITLE02 come from app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy:18-22, where the 'Credit Card Demo Application (CCDA)' literal is commented out at :21, so TITLE02O is the 40-byte CardDemo title actually in effect at :22. CURDATEO and CURTIMEO derive from FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE, so the clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:34 - the one instant shared by all twenty cases of this folder - and the code page is named explicitly as US-ASCII; neither is left to a platform default. The AID is stated as the IBM mnemonic DFHENTER, which is the spelling ParityCase validates against CicsAid.mnemonicsByAid(); PfKeyResolver.resolve maps that byte to AidKey.ENTER, so WHEN DFHENTER at :91 selects PROCESS-ENTER-KEY at :92 - reached at all because CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT is 1, which makes NOT CDEMO-PGM-REENTER at :83 false and drives RECEIVE-USRADD-SCREEN. Termination is EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID('CU01') COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) at :107-110, so the 160-byte commarea travels back in the payload with no server-side session state and nextProgram stays on this program instead of naming a transfer. On styling this case asserts nothing the program does not do: COUSR01C copies neither CSSETATY nor CSSTRPFY, and its COPY DFHATTR at :57 is commented out, so no '*' marker and no per-field DFHRED exists here to assert - the red on the message line is the map's own ERRMSG DFHMDF ATTRB=(ASKIP,BRT,FSET) COLOR=RED at app/bms/COUSR01.bms:151-154, which the program never writes. ERRMSGC is pinned to the default colour DFHDFCOL precisely because MOVE DFHGREEN TO ERRMSGC at :254 is the only colour assignment anywhere in the program and it belongs to the successful write, so a green message on this arm would mean a record had been written. PROVENANCE: every expected value above is STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of app/cbl/COUSR01C.cbl:83-110, :117-151, :142-147, :153-159, :184-196, :214-233 and :238-274, cross-checked against app/cpy-bms/COUSR01.CPY (USRTYPEI PIC X(1) at :84, USRTYPEO at :158, ERRMSGO PIC X(78) at :164, the REDEFINES at :91), app/bms/COUSR01.bms (the USRTYPE and ERRMSG DFHMDF definitions at :140-154), app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy:18-22, app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy and app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy for the header and commarea shapes, app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy:17-23 (8 + 20 + 20 + 8 + 1 + 23 = 80, with SEC-USR-FILLER PIC X(23) present and space-filled) and the ten inline rows of app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:L35-L44 at their JCL width of 57. They were NOT captured from a live COBOL execution. AAP 0.7.6 (risk R-A) documents eight independently verified blockers that make executing this program here impossible - no z/OS runtime, the available compiler's indexed file handler disabled, subprogram linkage that cannot produce an executable, a copybook that fails to parse, no Language Environment CEE services, no CICS emulator for the seventeen online programs, EBCDIC fixtures requiring binary handling, and no installable alternative compiler - so the provenance of these values is derivation from the sources cited, and the 560-case gate, the field-for-field diffing and the diff-count-of-zero requirement are preserved unchanged.
